memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly and revere your God. I am the LORD.'" - Lev 19:32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Stand up. It is a physical instruction — when an older person enters, get to your feet.

There is something wonderfully concrete about that. God does not say "value the elderly" in the abstract. He says: move your body. Show it.

And notice the last phrase: and revere your God. Respect for the aged and reverence for God are placed in the same breath, as though one flows naturally from the other.

Our culture struggles here. We prize youth, speed, and productivity, and we quietly sideline those who have less of all three. Older people become invisible — in workplaces, in families, sometimes in churches. Many live desperately lonely lives while surrounded by busy people.

Scripture consistently pushes the other way. Grey hair is a crown of splendour; it is attained in the way of righteousness (Prov 16:31). Paul told Timothy to treat older men as fathers (1 Tim 5:1). And the church is instructed to care properly for widows (1 Tim 5:3-4).

Think of one older person who has slipped from your attention. A neighbour. A relative. Someone from church who stopped coming and nobody followed up.

Stand up. Then go and see them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which older person in your life has slipped from your attention?
2. What does your culture teach you about ageing that Scripture contradicts?
3. What practical step could you take for an elderly person this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for overlooking those the world sidelines. Give me genuine respect for the elderly, and show me one person I can go and see this week. Amen.
